name: Humana Go365 device ecosystem (Validic-powered)
why: Go365, Humana's wellness and rewards program, publishes compatible-device lists for employer and Medicare members (Fitbit, Garmin, Withings, Polar, iHealth and others) and moved to Validic so members could connect hundreds of wearables. Humana Healthy Horizons in Ohio (Medicaid) also runs Go365 rewards.
ask: Ask Validic (Humana's device-connectivity vendor) what it takes for a new wearable to appear in the Go365 compatible-device list.
opener: Hi, I'm Jeremy at Vybe Health in Akron. We're building a screenless overnight ECG/HRV band with an open SDK, launching May 2027. Go365 already connects a long list of wearables through Validic. Could you point me to the right person to learn how a new device gets added to the Go365 compatible list? Happy to share a one-page overview.
geo: US (Humana HQ Louisville, KY); Go365 offered to Ohio Medicaid members
entry_route: Indirect: Go365 device connections run through Validic, so the route is becoming a Validic-supported device first, then asking Humana/Go365 to enable it. No public Humana device-partner form found.
opportunity: Get the Vybe band onto the Go365 compatible-device list so employer, Medicare and Ohio Medicaid members can earn Go365 points with it.
unknowns: Whether Humana enables every Validic device or curates the Go365 list; who at Humana owns device additions; current Go365 device list contents for 2026 (list is in an attachment we could not open); whether Go365 credits sleep/HRV or only steps.

name: Validic Inform (supported-device network for payers and health systems)
why: Validic says its platform supports 600-700+ wearables, medical devices and apps and integrates with EHRs; payers such as Humana (Go365) use it to connect member devices. Its help center says clients request new device additions through support.
ask: 15-minute call on what Validic needs from a device maker (API, data model, commercial terms) to list a new wearable.
opener: Hi, I'm Jeremy at Vybe Health in Akron, Ohio. We're building a screenless overnight ECG/HRV band with a licensed SDK and cloud API, launching May 2027. Several payers reach member wearables through Validic. Could we have 15 minutes to learn what Validic needs from a new device maker to become a supported integration? Happy to share our API docs.
entry_route: Validic help center: clients request new device additions through Validic support; device-maker partner program not found publicly. Start via the supported-devices page / contact.
opportunity: One integration into Validic could make Vybe connectable for every payer, employer-wellness and RPM client that uses Validic (Go365 is one).
unknowns: Whether device makers can self-initiate (help pages describe client requests); any fees; whether Validic requires an existing customer to request Vybe; data types Validic ingests beyond steps/sleep/HR.

name: UnitedHealthcare Rewards (compatible trackers incl. Oura and WHOOP)
why: UHC Rewards pays members for tracker-based daily activity and sleep goals; UHC's employer toolkit lists compatible trackers including Samsung, Oura Ring, WHOOP, Apple Watch, Fitbit and Garmin, showing it has added newer non-watch wearables over time.
ask: Find the UHC Rewards product/partnerships owner and ask what the bar is for adding a new compatible tracker.
opener: Hi, I'm Jeremy at Vybe Health in Akron, Ohio. We're building a screenless overnight band that tracks sleep and HRV, with an open SDK and no required subscription, launching May 2027. UHC Rewards already credits sleep tracking from rings and bands. Could you tell me how UHC evaluates adding a new compatible tracker, and who owns that decision?
entry_route: No public device-partner intake found; route is a named contact in UHC Rewards product/partnerships (warm intro or LinkedIn).
opportunity: Be listed as a UHC Rewards compatible tracker so employer-plan members can earn sleep and activity rewards with Vybe.
unknowns: Device onboarding process and criteria; whether UHC requires a sales history or volume; whether integration is direct or via Apple Health/Google Fit; contact owner.

name: Blue365 member discount program (Partner with Blue365)
why: Blue365 is the BCBS-wide health and wellness discount program (fitness gear among its categories); its FAQ says vendors apply through the 'Partner with Blue365' form. It cites 5M+ members and 90+ national brand partners.
ask: Submit the Partner with Blue365 form for a member discount on the Vybe band at consumer launch.
opener: Hi, I'm Jeremy at Vybe Health in Akron, Ohio. We're launching a screenless overnight sleep and HRV band in May 2027, one-time purchase with no required subscription. We'd like to offer Blue Cross Blue Shield members a Blue365 discount at launch. What does Blue365 look for in a new fitness-gear partner, and when should a launching brand apply?
geo: US (national BCBS program; Anthem is the Blue plan in Ohio)
entry_route: Public 'Partner with Blue365' form (FAQ: use the Additional Information field to describe products).
opportunity: Member-discount listing for the band across BCBS plans, a low-cost consumer channel at the May 2027 launch.
unknowns: Discount depth or fees expected; approval criteria; whether pre-launch brands are accepted; review timeline. Program stats come from Blue365's own materials.

name: Wellhub (formerly Gympass) Wellness App partner program
why: Wellhub sells a corporate wellness subscription to employers and lists 'wellness apps' as a partner type; its help center says app makers register by choosing the Wellness App option, and joining is free with no registration fee. Wellhub is also a certified partner on Personify Health's marketplace.
ask: Register Vybe's companion app as a Wellhub Wellness App partner once the app is live; meanwhile ask how hardware-linked apps are handled.
opener: Hi, I'm Jeremy at Vybe Health in Akron, Ohio. We're launching a screenless overnight sleep and HRV band and companion app in May 2027, no required subscription. Wellhub lists wellness apps as partners for employer members. Does Wellhub accept apps that pair with a wearable, and what would a launch-stage app need to qualify?
entry_route: Public partner registration: wellhub.com/en-us/partners -> select 'Wellness App'.
opportunity: Put Vybe's app (and a band offer) in front of employer-sponsored Wellhub members as a listed wellness app.
unknowns: Whether apps that require purchased hardware are accepted; revenue model for app partners; review criteria; whether a device discount can be offered inside Wellhub.

name: WebMD Health Services ONE Integrations (formerly Limeade)
why: WebMD Health Services (which acquired Limeade) says its ONE platform is compatible with 250+ activity trackers, medical devices and apps (Apple Health, Fitbit, Garmin, Polar, Withings, Strava and others) feeding employer well-being programs. SummaCare (Akron) offers members WebMD Health Manager.
ask: Ask WebMD Health Services how a new device joins ONE Integrations (direct vs via Apple Health).
opener: Hi, I'm Jeremy at Vybe Health in Akron, Ohio. We're building a screenless overnight sleep and HRV band with an open API, launching May 2027. ONE already pulls data from hundreds of devices into employer well-being programs. Could you point me to whoever manages device integrations, so I can learn what a new wearable needs to be supported?
entry_route: ONE Integrations solution page (contact); no device-maker partner form found.
opportunity: Become a supported ONE device so employer participants (and plans like SummaCare using WebMD tools) can sync Vybe sleep/activity data for program credit.
unknowns: Whether new direct integrations are being added or only via Apple Health/Health Connect; metrics accepted (steps, sleep hours, exercise minutes per Limeade support); commercial terms.

name: Sharecare (tracker sync via Apple Health / Health Connect)
why: Sharecare's help center says it supports devices that write to Apple Health, Google Fit/Health Connect, Samsung Health and Fitbit for steps and sleep; employers and plans (e.g. Emory, Health Net, CareFirst) use Sharecare tracker linking for wellness credit.
ask: Confirm Vybe sleep/steps written to Apple Health and Health Connect flow into Sharecare; then ask Sharecare about a named listing.
opener: Hi, I'm Jeremy at Vybe Health in Akron, Ohio. We're launching a screenless overnight sleep and HRV band in May 2027 that writes to Apple Health and Health Connect. Many employers run Sharecare tracker credit. Is there a way for a new device to be named in Sharecare's supported list, or is the Health app route the intended path?
entry_route: Zero-integration route: write sleep and steps to Apple Health / Health Connect, which Sharecare reads. Named-device partnership: no public form found.
opportunity: Day-one compatibility with Sharecare-run employer and health-plan wellness programs by writing to the phone health stores, then pursue a named listing.
unknowns: Whether Sharecare reads HRV or only steps/sleep; whether named listing matters to employers; partner contact.

name: Anthem Sydney Health app rewards (Ohio public employers, e.g. Union County / CEBCO)
org: Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield (Elevance Health)
why: Union County, Ohio's benefit materials say Anthem's Sydney Health app connects directly with Fitbit, Garmin, iHealth, Misfit, Apple HealthKit and Google Fit, and any other device indirectly via the phone health app; the CEBCO Rewards program pays members for connecting a tracker and step goals.
ask: Confirm Vybe data reaches Sydney via HealthKit/Google Health Connect; then ask an Ohio county benefits/wellness coordinator about piloting the band in a CEBCO wellness challenge.
opener: Hi, I'm Jeremy at Vybe Health in Akron. We're building a screenless overnight sleep and HRV band, launching May 2027, that syncs to Apple Health and Health Connect. Your Sydney rewards program credits connected trackers. Would your wellness team be open to a short conversation about a small employee pilot once our devices ship?
entry_route: Indirect device route via the phone health app (documented in the Union County PDF); pilot route via county HR/wellness coordinators. No Anthem device-partner form found.
opportunity: Ohio public employers on Anthem can credit Vybe-tracked steps through the phone health app with no Anthem integration; a county or CEBCO pilot is a local reference customer.
unknowns: Whether indirect (HealthKit) data earns the same rewards as direct devices; whether Sydney uses sleep data; current plan-year rules; named HR contacts not found.

name: AultCare Health + Wellness app (Canton, OH)
why: AultCare, a Canton, Ohio health plan, describes its Health + Wellness app as connecting to health apps and wearables plus Bluetooth medical devices for lifestyle monitoring, alongside employer wellness programs and monthly fitness initiatives.

opener: Hi, I'm Jeremy at Vybe Health, 25 miles up the road in Akron. We're building a screenless overnight sleep and HRV band, launching May 2027. Your Health + Wellness app connects to wearables for employer wellness programs. Could I learn which devices you support today and whether a Northeast Ohio device would be worth piloting with one of your employer groups?
entry_route: No device-partner page; reach via AultCare contact listed in the Canton Regional Chamber directory, or via the Canton Chamber network.
opportunity: Regional health plan next door to Akron; employer groups with monthly fitness initiatives are natural small pilots.
unknowns: Which wearables the app integrates (not listed in results); whether it reads Apple Health/Health Connect; wellness contact name.

name: HealthCheck360 supported devices (Dubuque, IA)

ask: Ask HealthCheck360 how a new device joins its supported list and whether Apple Health/Health Connect sync is enough.
opener: Hi, I'm Jeremy at Vybe Health in Akron, Ohio. We're building a screenless overnight sleep and HRV band with an open API, launching May 2027. HealthCheck360's supported-devices list covers a lot of Midwest employers. Could you tell me how you decide to add a new wearable, and whether Health app sync is the usual route?
entry_route: Supported-devices page; no explicit partner form seen. Indirect route via Apple Health.
opportunity: Midwest employer-wellness vendor whose clients could credit Vybe activity/sleep via Apple Health now and a direct listing later.
unknowns: Whether its device list is powered by an aggregator (several listed brands suggest one); data types credited; partner contact.

name: Sonic Boom Wellness supported devices
why: Sonic Boom's help center lists compatible devices (Fitbit, Apple Watch, Garmin, Samsung, Strava, Apple Health, Samsung Health Connect) for its employer wellness platform, which serves healthcare and other employers; it even shipped its own tracker (Boomerang).
ask: Confirm Health Connect / Apple Health route works for Vybe data; ask about a named listing.
opener: Hi, I'm Jeremy at Vybe Health in Akron, Ohio. We're launching a screenless overnight sleep and HRV band in May 2027 that syncs to Apple Health and Health Connect. Sonic Boom already credits several trackers for employer programs. What does it take for a new wearable to be added to your compatible-device list?
entry_route: Indirect via Apple Health / Samsung Health Connect (listed as compatible); direct listing via company contact.
opportunity: Compatibility with Sonic Boom employer challenges (including healthcare employers) from launch.
unknowns: Whether sleep/HRV is credited or only steps; partner process; contact owner.

name: YuMuuv wellness challenge platform
why: YuMuuv, a team wellness-challenge platform, lists direct integrations with Apple Health, Health Connect, Garmin (via Garmin Health API), Fitbit, Polar, Suunto, and also Oura, Strava and Withings; other devices connect indirectly through Apple Health/Health Connect.
ask: Ask YuMuuv whether it adds direct device integrations on request and test the Health Connect route.
opener: Hi, I'm Jeremy at Vybe Health in Akron, Ohio. We're building a screenless overnight band with an open API, launching May 2027. YuMuuv already connects Oura, Garmin and others for team challenges. Would you consider a direct integration with a new band, or is Health Connect / Apple Health the path you'd recommend?
entry_route: Indirect via Apple Health/Health Connect (documented); direct integration by contacting YuMuuv (no partner form found).
opportunity: Instant participation in employer step/activity challenges, then a direct integration for richer data.
unknowns: Size of US customer base; whether YuMuuv builds integrations on request; partner terms.

Henry Ford previously ran an employee wearable-tech idea competition.
ask: Apply to Pitch @ Henry Ford (or the current challenge if it fits) proposing a small sleep/HRV wellness pilot with staff.
opener: Hi, I'm Jeremy at Vybe Health in Akron, Ohio. We're building a screenless overnight ECG/HRV band and developer platform, launching May 2027. Henry Ford's early-stage program mentions pilots and co-development with startups. Would a 15-minute call make sense to see whether a small wellness pilot fits Pitch @ Henry Ford or a current challenge?
entry_route: Named program: Early-Stage Company Engagement (Pitch @ Henry Ford; Competitions apply page).
opportunity: Midwest health-system pilot partner and reference site; possible fund conversation later.
unknowns: Current challenge topic and dates (not read); whether general-wellness (non-clinical) products qualify; pilot budgets.

opener: Hi, I'm Jeremy at Vybe Health in Akron, Ohio. We're building a screenless overnight sleep and HRV band with an open SDK for researchers, launching May 2027. Innovation Ventures mentions piloting external solutions. Could we have a short call to see whether a small, non-clinical wellness pilot or research collaboration fits your process?
entry_route: Collaborate page (Innovation Ventures) - external piloting and co-development route.
opportunity: Ohio health-system pilot or research collaboration using the DevKit.
unknowns: No evidence of a current wearable program at Cincinnati Children's; pediatric use would need age-appropriate design and IRB; contact person not identified.

opener: Hi, I'm Jeremy at Vybe Health, an Akron startup building a screenless overnight sleep and HRV band, launching May 2027. Your innovation center pilots new approaches here at home. Would you be open to a short conversation about whether a small, non-clinical staff-wellness pilot could fit, and who the right person would be?
entry_route: Center for Patient Experience Innovation (pilot site) and Research Collaborations page; hospital site mentions a 'Submit an Idea' option (could not confirm it accepts outside vendors).
opportunity: Hometown health-system pilot for staff sleep/recovery wellness; strong local reference.
unknowns: Whether external companies can submit to the innovation center; no wearable program found; contact not identified; Becker's listing date unknown.

Burnalong already syncs several wearables for employer and health-plan members. Would you be open to a short call about adding a recovery-focused device or a co-marketing pilot?

Rally/Optum Engage connects member trackers for incentive programs. Could you point me to who decides on adding new devices, and what they look for?

SilverSneakers GO already connects Fitbit for members. Would you be open to a conversation about adding a simple sleep-focused band, and who would own that?
